title: Latent Cluster Analysis for Vision-Language-Action Models
action_head: flow/diffusion action expert (DiT with cross-attention to Eagle VLM tokens, 4 denoising steps)
methods: agglomerative clustering of mean-pooled embeddings (last VLM layer and every DiT cross-attention layer per denoising step)
cross-attention-based token reweighting of VLM embeddings
Jaccard and overlap coefficient across layers
VLM-generated cluster concepts (LLaVA-72B) scored with CLIPSIM
question: Does clustering GR00T N1.5's backbone and action-decoder embeddings, with tokens reweighted by cross-attention, reveal interpretable structure in how actions are denoised?
key_findings: Cross-attention weighting raises mean Silhouette from 0.084 to 0.136 without PCA (+62.1%) and from 0.132 to 0.164 with PCA (+24.0%); Davies-Bouldin improves ~8% (Table 1).
Without PCA or weighting, clustering degenerates: 15,704 +/- 10,282 clusters from 24,000 samples; weighted+PCA gives ~7 clusters (Table 1).
Cluster counts fall at later denoising steps and deeper decoder layers, read as the latent space becoming more structured.
Cluster assignments are consistent across denoising steps within a layer (diagonal patterns in overlap matrices).
DiT-layer clusters separate episode timestep and arm displacement more than backbone clusters (~20% higher mean Wasserstein distance for arm joints).
Concept labels score CLIPSIM 0.206-0.233 across layers and configurations, with small differences; concepts are mostly variants of 'pick object and place in container' (Table 2).

benchmarks: GR00T X-Embodiment Sim subset of Open X-Embodiment (24 tasks)
evidence.scale: 1,000 embeddings per task x 24 tasks = 24,000 samples, consecutive samples 10 frames apart; concepts from top-5 samples for the 10 largest clusters per layer
evidence.statistics: partial: mean +/- std of cluster metrics across layers; no significance tests, no seeds

causal_validation: No. No ablation, steering or patching; clusters and concepts are descriptive.
closed_loop: No. Embeddings come from forward passes on recorded dataset clips.
limitations_stated: Concept generation lacks ground truth; concepts from static frames miss dynamics.
Short input horizon; findings may not extend to long-horizon behavior.
Agglomerative clustering assumptions may not fit non-spherical manifolds.
critique: The 'weighted' representation is the VLM backbone tokens rescaled by cross-attention weights, not the action-decoder hidden states. Comparing its cluster metrics with unweighted decoder embeddings compares different objects, so the 62% Silhouette gain is not evidence about the decoder.
Silhouette scores of 0.08-0.16 indicate weak cluster structure overall; clustering quality metrics also do not measure interpretability.
CLIPSIM differences of ~0.01-0.02 between configurations are within the reported std and carry no clear meaning; the generated concepts are near-duplicates.
Claims of 'spatiotemporal awareness' rest on clusters correlating with episode timestep, which is trivially expected when consecutive frames of the same episode are clustered.
Methodologically the weakest paper in the probing set; useful mainly as an example of descriptive clustering without validation.
one_line: Clustering GR00T N1.5's backbone and diffusion-decoder embeddings, with backbone tokens reweighted by cross-attention, gives somewhat tidier clusters that track timestep and arm motion, but the analysis is descriptive and its metrics say little about interpretability.
